[D1]
Find the mathematical function skeletons for the time derivatives of two co-evolving
scalar fields in a one-dimensional system: one broad field that spreads and saturates,
and one localized field that decays.

[V1]
u and v are scalar state fields. x is the spatial coordinate. t is time. u_t and v_t are
the time derivatives of u and v.

[D1: weak phenomenological description]
A nonnegative population-density field over two spatial coordinates evolves in
time. Observed patterns shift while their magnitude and smoothness change.
If a candidate proposes an external input, express it explicitly using x, y, t
and fitted constants; no additional input field is observed.
Do not assume any named PDE, reaction law, exact solution or forcing formula.
[V1: variable roles]
u is the observed density; x and y are spatial coordinates; t is time.
The target is the local temporal rate u_t. Spatial derivatives are estimated
from observations; no analytic time derivative or external input is supplied.
